prose_blocks:
The Reality Check: How It Works

Equity Release allows homeowners aged 55+ to unlock tax-free cash from their home. The most common type is the Lifetime Mortgage. You retain ownership of the home, and the loan is repaid when you die or move into long-term care.

The Compound Interest Trap

Unlike a normal mortgage where you pay off the interest monthly, here the interest is added to the loan. Next month, you pay interest on the interest.

Example: Borrow £50k at 6%.
Year 1: You owe £53,000.
Year 15: You owe £120,000.
This creates a "Snowball Effect" that eats into the inheritance you plan to leave behind.

The "No Negative Equity" Guarantee

There is a safety net. The Equity Release Council standards ensure you (or your estate) will never owe more than the property is worth.

If the debt grows to £500k, but the house sells for £400k, the lender writes off the £100k loss. Your family will not inherit a debt, but they might inherit £0.

Key Risks to Consider

  • Early Repayment Charges (ERCs): These can be huge. Some lenders charge up to 25% of the loan if you try to pay it off early within the first few years. Only do this if you plan to keep the loan for life.
  • Means Tested Benefits: Having £50,000 cash in the bank might disqualify you from Council Tax Support or Pension Credit.
  • Moving Home: You can usually "port" the mortgage to a new home, but the new property must meet the lender's criteria. Retirement flats are often rejected.
